architecture_basis.public_authority: CHARTER.md defines project scope and invariant principles; protocol and implementation details remain non-normative until accepted RFCs and ADRs bind them.
assumptions: The research evaluates the mission design of one role-separated Go artifact, PostgreSQL 17, external or local key custody, optional analyzers, and separate policy enforcement points.
Controls described here are candidate requirements for later RFCs and implementation tests, not evidence that production code exists or has passed them.
reopen_triggers: accepted RFC or ADR changes a process, store, trust boundary, key class, egress rule, lifecycle rule, or degraded-decision invariant

methodology: Model the approved architecture as data flows crossing named trust boundaries; treat the network, runtime, database, key provider, analyzer, operator, and recovery authority as separately compromisable.
Apply STRIDE to security properties and LINDDUN to privacy properties. A category is a prompt for analysis, not proof that a threat exists.
Map each stable threat to assets, actors, boundary, preconditions, mitigations, concrete validation, accountable owner, residual risk, and disposition.
Separate observed provider and standards behavior from Testament design inferences. External provider declarations are configuration evidence, not cryptographic proof of provider internals.
Assume authorized but fallible administrators, malicious tenants, compromised credentials, hostile trace content, unavailable dependencies, and a possible runtime compromise.

trust_boundaries.name: Producer to ingest edge
limitations: TLS does not establish that submitted content is benign or correctly attributed.

trust_boundaries.name: Runtime plaintext to persistence
sides: PostgreSQL, WAL, replicas, backups, and temporary persistence
limitations: A compromised authorized runtime can observe plaintext before encryption; application encryption is not end-to-end protection from that runtime.

trust_boundaries.name: Organization isolation
sides: another organization context and shared infrastructure
limitations: RLS is defense in depth and cannot contain arbitrary SQL executed by a sufficiently compromised privileged runtime.

trust_boundaries.name: Runtime to key provider
sides: AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, or development provider
crossings: plaintext organization roots inside mutually authenticated provider API requests
wrapped organization roots returned to or loaded from Testament
canonical provider key identifiers and versions
limitations: Cloud KMS custody requires critical keying material to cross into the selected provider over TLS; isolated-sovereign means no trace content egress, not no external key-custody boundary.
Provider availability, authorization, deletion, administrators, and hidden service internals remain outside Testament control.

trust_boundaries.name: Host to trusted built-in analyzer
sides: role-specific analyzer process with explicitly inventoried host capabilities
built-in deterministic, statistical, classifier, or local-model code
controls: run built-ins in a role-separated process
no provider credentials unless the egress broker mediates a separately authorized call
limitations: In-process built-ins inherit that role process capabilities; they are trusted code and are not a sandbox boundary.

trust_boundaries.name: Egress broker to external provider
controls: no redirects or fallback outside policy
limitations: Testament can evidence what it sends and the configured provider terms; it cannot verify undisclosed provider processing or compel deletion.

trust_boundaries.name: Operator client to query and console
limitations: An authorized endpoint or operator can exfiltrate displayed plaintext; client compromise is outside application encryption.

trust_boundaries.name: Policy decision to enforcement point
sides: Testament deterministic policy and receipt signer
limitations: A receipt does not enforce anything when a resource server ignores it or exposes a bypass path.

trust_boundaries.name: Deployment operator and break-glass control
controls: two-person or step-up controls for destructive actions
limitations: Host root can alter binaries or memory and is not contained by in-process controls.

trust_boundaries.name: Backup to restore and recovery authority
sides: restored deployment plus separately protected recovery authority
limitations: Residual backup ciphertext can remain after active-system erasure; destroyed keys and missing authority may make restoration impossible.

trust_boundaries.name: Source and supply chain to release
sides: contributors, dependencies, CI, and build inputs
limitations: A compromised trusted maintainer or signing environment can undermine the release unless independent verification detects it.

trust_boundaries.name: Public standards site
sides: static public research and normative documents
crossings: none by design; only versioned public artifacts are published
controls: no deployment credentials or data path
limitations: Publication can still disclose material accidentally committed to public artifacts.

trust_boundaries.name: Host operating system and role process
sides: kernel, container, service manager, and host root
crossings: binary, environment, file descriptors, memory, signals, crash state, network namespace
limitations: Host root, kernel, hypervisor, or firmware compromise can observe or alter process plaintext and keys.

trust_boundaries.name: Identity provider and verifier
crossings: issuer metadata, public verification keys, token claims, revocation and certificate status
controls: no forwarded identity from untrusted proxies
limitations: A compromised trusted issuer can mint valid identities; Testament cannot repair issuer governance.

trust_boundaries.name: Operational observability provider
crossings: fixed-schema content-excluding logs, metrics, traces, health, and alert metadata
controls: no request bodies, prompts, credentials, content-derived labels, or DEKs
limitations: Identifiers, timing, topology, and error metadata remain sensitive and can support linkage even without content fields.

trust_boundaries.name: Managed database, replica, and backup operator
sides: database service, replicas, snapshots, object media, and provider administrators
crossings: ciphertext, wrapped DEKs, blind indexes, bounded metadata, tombstones, and backup manifests
controls: forced RLS as defense in depth
limitations: Provider administrators can delete or roll back ciphertext and metadata; they must not be assumed to preserve availability or chronology.

trust_boundaries.name: Isolated extension analyzer runtime
sides: host broker and read-only content handles
crossings: bounded input handles, configuration, deadline and budgets, schema-constrained output
controls: no ambient network, database, environment, KMS, credentials, or writable host filesystem
CPU, memory, fuel, time, input, and output limits
limitations: OS and sandbox defects can break isolation; this is not a perfect hostile multi-tenant boundary.

data_inventory.name: Exact accepted source bytes
data_inventory.source: authorized producers through API, CLI, file, or stdin
data_inventory.sensitivity: potentially confidential, personal, regulated, secret-bearing, or harmful
data_inventory.purpose: authoritative custody, replay, review, and provenance
data_inventory.storage: application-encrypted, independently authenticated chunks plus final manifest
data_inventory.egress: none unless an explicit profile and operation authorize exact content
data_inventory.retention: organization rule measured from recorded acceptance time and constrained by holds
data_inventory.deletion: deny active reads, delete active lineage, then cryptographic erasure where eligible; report backups separately

data_inventory.name: Decoded and parsed representations
data_inventory.sensitivity: same as or more revealing than source content
data_inventory.storage: versioned encrypted derived artifacts linked to exact source
data_inventory.egress: profile-authorized only; never treated as safer merely because it is derived
data_inventory.retention: no longer than governing source unless a reviewed independent purpose applies
data_inventory.deletion: deleted with source lineage and recorded in the deletion operation

data_inventory.name: Findings, summaries, features, and entity links
data_inventory.sensitivity: content-bearing, inferential, potentially discriminatory, and possibly wrong
data_inventory.purpose: analysis, triage, longitudinal review, and policy input
data_inventory.egress: only within the selected analyzer profile and authorized review or export scope
data_inventory.retention: lineage-aware rule with appeal and review needs explicitly balanced
data_inventory.deletion: remove with governed lineage; preserve only content-free tombstone and audit evidence

data_inventory.name: Human annotations, appeals, and case records
data_inventory.source: reviewers, affected parties, and accountable authorities
data_inventory.sensitivity: personal, employment-related, legal, security-sensitive, and inferential
data_inventory.egress: minimum authorized review or legal disclosure scope
data_inventory.retention: versioned case rule; holds and procedural obligations override ordinary expiry
data_inventory.deletion: delete content when eligible while retaining minimal content-free accountability record

data_inventory.name: Identity, membership, and authorization data
data_inventory.source: configured identity issuers and local administration
data_inventory.storage: minimum identifiers and encrypted sensitive attributes
data_inventory.egress: identity protocol and explicit administration only
data_inventory.retention: membership lifecycle plus security audit requirements
data_inventory.deletion: revoke authority immediately; delete eligible profile data without breaking immutable attribution

data_inventory.name: Provider and service credentials
data_inventory.source: organization administrators through write-only credential paths
data_inventory.purpose: authorized KMS, identity, or external analyzer operations
data_inventory.storage: encrypted under the organization secret root; no readback
data_inventory.egress: inserted only into the authorized destination request
data_inventory.retention: until rotation, revocation, organization deletion, or configured expiry
data_inventory.deletion: revoke externally where supported, erase local wrapped material, report external state

data_inventory.name: Cryptographic key material and wrapped roots
data_inventory.source: cryptographic RNG and configured key provider
data_inventory.purpose: data, search, secret, and audit protection
data_inventory.storage: provider-custodied top key and application-wrapped purpose-separated organization roots
data_inventory.egress: Cloud custody sends one 32-byte plaintext organization root only through the selected exact AWS, GCP, or Azure egress schema and receives one bounded wrapped root; payload DEKs and trace plaintext do not cross this boundary.
data_inventory.retention: generation dependency graph; held or referenced generations cannot retire
data_inventory.deletion: controlled destruction only after dependency and hold proof

data_inventory.name: Blind indexes and entity tokens
data_inventory.source: normalized selected values under organization- and field-scoped search root
data_inventory.purpose: narrow equality search and tenant-local correlation
data_inventory.egress: never to external analyzer unless explicitly authorized as derived metadata
data_inventory.retention: same governing lineage as indexed content
data_inventory.deletion: remove with content and reindex or retire during root rotation

data_inventory.name: Policy decisions, receipts, and obligations
data_inventory.sensitivity: security-sensitive; may expose activity or findings
data_inventory.storage: immutable signed or integrity-bound records with sensitive fields encrypted
data_inventory.egress: short-lived receipt to the declared audience; no raw evidence unless contract requires and authorizes it
data_inventory.retention: policy and audit rule independent of receipt expiry
data_inventory.deletion: preserve minimum audit integrity while deleting content-bearing references when eligible

data_inventory.name: Audit entries and checkpoints
data_inventory.source: consequential operations and security-relevant reads or denials
data_inventory.sensitivity: content-excluding but security- and privacy-sensitive metadata; identifiers, hashes, time, and hold scope can be linkable
data_inventory.purpose: attribution, tamper evidence, investigation, and recovery comparison
data_inventory.storage: per-organization hash chain and signed checkpoints
data_inventory.retention: separate accountable audit schedule and holds
data_inventory.deletion: never silently rewrite chain; use superseding/tombstone evidence under an approved rule

data_inventory.name: Operational logs, metrics, and traces
data_inventory.sensitivity: non-content operational metadata with identifiers bounded for cardinality
data_inventory.purpose: health, debugging, performance, and security monitoring
data_inventory.deletion: provider-specific expiry or deletion reported independently

data_inventory.name: Exports, downloads, and caches
data_inventory.source: authorized derived copies of governed data
data_inventory.sensitivity: inherits all source sensitivity and adds redistribution risk
data_inventory.storage: application-encrypted cache or export object; local output is restrictive, atomic, and remains encrypted until the authorized client consumes it
data_inventory.egress: only to the authorized requester and destination
data_inventory.retention: short explicit expiry no longer than source authority
data_inventory.deletion: revoke capability, remove active copy, and report recipient or external persistence as outside direct control

data_inventory.name: Retention rules, legal holds, tombstones, and recovery manifests
data_inventory.source: authorized administrators, legal process, deletion operations, and external recovery authority
data_inventory.sensitivity: security and legal metadata; scope can reveal subject activity
data_inventory.purpose: govern lifecycle, prevent deletion, block rollback, and prove residual state
data_inventory.storage: versioned, signed or integrity-bound, organization-scoped control records
data_inventory.egress: authorized legal, audit, backup, or recovery process only
data_inventory.retention: at least through all governed dependencies and recovery windows
data_inventory.deletion: only by a separately authorized process that preserves anti-rollback and audit requirements

data_inventory.name: Plaintext process memory and crash state
data_inventory.source: authorized decryption, parsing, analysis, policy, or reveal inside a role process
data_inventory.sensitivity: inherits the highest sensitivity of active content and keys
data_inventory.storage: no intentional persistence; swap, core dumps, crash uploads, and spill are disabled or encrypted and inventoried
data_inventory.egress: none except authorized response to an in-boundary client
data_inventory.retention: bounded by operation lifetime and best-effort zeroization
data_inventory.deletion: release buffers and keys promptly; verify no durable crash or spill artifact

data_inventory.name: External provider retained request, response, and metadata
data_inventory.sensitivity: inherits outbound content plus provider identifiers and usage metadata
data_inventory.purpose: declared analyzer, key-custody, or identity operation
data_inventory.egress: already outside the deployment at the declared provider boundary
data_inventory.retention: exact provider, endpoint, account, and contract declaration; unknown is not zero
data_inventory.deletion: request provider deletion where supported and report pending, unsupported, or unknown separately

data_inventory.name: Client, browser, clipboard, network, DNS, and TLS metadata
data_inventory.source: operator queries, reveals, downloads, and all network connections
data_inventory.sensitivity: content may appear in authorized client memory; metadata can identify activity
data_inventory.storage: organization-managed endpoint, browser, proxy, DNS, and network systems
data_inventory.egress: only within the profile boundary; an out-of-boundary client is a governed transfer
data_inventory.retention: organization endpoint and network policy with explicit cache and history controls
data_inventory.deletion: application revokes capability but cannot erase an uncontrolled recipient endpoint

data_inventory.name: Queues, parser spill, support bundles, and diagnostic artifacts
data_inventory.source: background work, oversized processing, or support workflow
data_inventory.purpose: only an explicitly approved bounded operation
data_inventory.storage: production defaults forbid plaintext spill and ad hoc support bundles; any durable queue payload is application encrypted
data_inventory.egress: none without a separate governed export
data_inventory.retention: explicit short operation TTL with no implicit default
data_inventory.deletion: cancel and erase with source lineage; report any external recipient separately

controls.title: Strict identity and organization binding
controls.requirement: Validate issuers, credentials, server-derived organization, and scoped tokens with deny-by-default authorization.

controls.title: Authenticated evidence and immutable history
controls.requirement: Authenticate chunks/manifests, preserve versions, sign receipts/checkpoints, and require external anti-rollback authority.

controls.title: Transactional attributable audit
controls.requirement: Commit content-excluding organization-scoped audit atomically with consequential actions and preserve separate decision/enforcement evidence.

controls.title: Application encryption and leak prevention
controls.requirement: Encrypt content before persistence and exclude plaintext, prompts, credentials, and DEKs from observability and durable temporary surfaces.

controls.title: Bounded resources and tenant fairness
controls.requirement: Bound reads, expansion, parsing, graph traversal, analyzers, retries, budgets, and per-tenant concurrency.

controls.title: Role and analyzer capability confinement
controls.requirement: Use role processes, generated permissions, brokered handles, purpose-separated keys, and isolated extension runtimes.

controls.title: Host validation of untrusted content and output
controls.requirement: Separate instructions from evidence, validate schemas and exact evidence references, render as text, and keep deterministic policy authoritative.

controls.title: Explicit profile and destination enforcement
controls.requirement: Require a profile, field and destination allowlists, per-attempt reauthorization, no silent fallback, and observable egress attempts.

controls.title: Truthful degraded-decision semantics
controls.requirement: Separate evaluation availability, effective action, and actual enforcement; never label degraded allow as safe or passed.

controls.title: Scoped correlation and equality tokens
controls.requirement: Scope tokens and entity graphs by organization, field, purpose, and generation; forbid cross-organization content correlation.

controls.title: Purpose-bound minimization and reveal
controls.requirement: Collect, derive, reveal, and export only authorized fields; mask by default and treat derived data as potentially identifying.

controls.title: Attributable appeal and correction
controls.requirement: Preserve uncertainty, delegation, counterevidence, appeal, correction, and supersession without rewriting source history.

controls.title: Non-enumerating access surfaces
controls.requirement: Use opaque scoped capabilities, bounded errors, and measured response equivalence for absent and foreign resources.

controls.title: Explicit attestations and change history
controls.requirement: Require signed profile and lifecycle declarations with no default, widening confirmation, limits, and accessible history.

controls.title: Fenced lineage-aware lifecycle
controls.requirement: Bind fixed clocks, rule/hold epochs, lineage closure, resumable deletion, provider states, tombstones, and external recovery authority.

controls.title: Pinned reviewed supply chain
controls.requirement: Protect source review, pin actions/tools/dependencies, scan licenses/secrets, and bind SBOM, provenance, and release signatures.

controls.title: Static-site publication separation
controls.requirement: Keep the public site outside deployment data paths and scan every published artifact for private references and secrets.

threats.title: Foreign organization or actor identity is accepted
preconditions: credential, forwarded claim, resource identifier, or pool context can influence effective organization
threats.scenario: An attacker presents or smuggles a foreign identity or organization selector and Testament attributes the request to a more privileged principal.
mitigations: validate issuer, audience, time, subject, and transport identity
bind API keys, cursors, sessions, receipts, and idempotency to organization and authorization
clear transaction-local context on every path
validations: 1,000 alternating two-organization requests through a pool of one
forged header, body, cursor, and token matrix
threats.residual_risk: A compromised trusted issuer or runtime can mint or reinterpret identity; external issuer security remains required.
threats.treatment_deadline: before production implementation for the affected boundary
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: accountable maintainer plus non-author security/privacy reviewer; critical or high review findings are not waivable at the research gate

validations: bit mutation, truncation, reorder, duplicate, substitution, and wrong-context matrix

preconditions: direct identifiers or a combination of quasi-identifiers is present or inferred
threats.scenario: A person, employee, customer, minor, patient, or sensitive actor is identified beyond the declared purpose or authorization.
mitigations: deterministic redaction where profile permits only derived data
no claim that pseudonymization equals anonymization
validations: export manifest and opposite-organization canary scan
threats.residual_risk: Free-form traces can contain identifiers in unexpected fields; inference and re-identification cannot be ruled out.
threats.treatment_deadline: before production implementation for the affected boundary
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: accountable maintainer plus non-author security/privacy reviewer; critical or high review findings are not waivable at the research gate

threats.title: Accountability evidence becomes disproportionate proof against a person
preconditions: strongly attributable records are retained or interpreted beyond their stated purpose and uncertainty
threats.scenario: Tamper-evident records prevent plausible deniability or are treated as proof of human intent even though an agent, shared account, compromise, or model produced the action.
mitigations: record actor type, delegation, confidence, and counterevidence
state that signatures prove record integrity, not human intent
threats.residual_risk: Accountability and privacy goals conflict; applicable law and organizational policy determine the acceptable balance.
threats.treatment_deadline: before production implementation for the affected boundary
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: accountable maintainer plus non-author security/privacy reviewer; critical or high review findings are not waivable at the research gate

threats.title: Presence, absence, or activity is detectable without content access
preconditions: errors, timing, identifiers, sizes, pagination, quotas, or external calls differ based on protected activity
threats.scenario: An observer infers that a person, trace, investigation, hold, finding, or organization exists.
mitigations: padding only where justified by measured risk
threats.residual_risk: Traffic volume, ciphertext length, and operational timing can remain observable; Testament does not promise general traffic-flow confidentiality.
threats.treatment_deadline: before production implementation for the affected boundary
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: accountable maintainer plus non-author security/privacy reviewer; critical or high review findings are not waivable at the research gate

threats.title: Protected data is revealed to an unauthorized or unintended recipient
preconditions: authorization, encryption, key binding, output handling, or destination control fails
threats.scenario: Source, derived content, identity, secret, or lifecycle metadata is disclosed through query, export, backup, provider, logs, or key misuse.
threats.residual_risk: Authorized users and runtimes can intentionally disclose what they may read; organizational endpoint and personnel controls remain necessary.
threats.treatment_deadline: before production implementation for the affected boundary
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: accountable maintainer plus non-author security/privacy reviewer; critical or high review findings are not waivable at the research gate

threats.title: Data subject or organization cannot understand processing and egress
preconditions: setup defaults, hidden fallback, vague labels, missing notices, or inaccessible evidence obscure what is collected, inferred, retained, or sent
threats.scenario: An organization selects a configuration without understanding content classes, destinations, retention, degraded behavior, provider limits, or later profile widening.
validations: empty and unknown setup values fail without state
profile transition and UI label tests
threats.residual_risk: Complex processing cannot be reduced to one notice; organizations remain responsible for lawful, contextual communication.
threats.treatment_deadline: before production implementation for the affected boundary
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: accountable maintainer plus non-author security/privacy reviewer; critical or high review findings are not waivable at the research gate

threats.title: Processing violates declared purpose, retention, transfer, or legal obligation
preconditions: rules, jurisdiction, contracts, holds, provider behavior, or deletion obligations are incomplete, stale, conflicting, or unenforced
threats.scenario: Data is retained too long, deleted despite hold, transferred outside the declared boundary, restored after deletion, or processed for an incompatible purpose.
validations: overlapping hold and deletion race matrix
threats.owner: organization privacy and legal owner with Testament lifecycle maintainer
threats.residual_risk: Testament supplies technical controls and evidence, not legal advice or universal compliance; obligations vary and provider claims can change.
threats.treatment_deadline: before production implementation for the affected boundary
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: accountable maintainer plus non-author security/privacy reviewer; critical or high review findings are not waivable at the research gate

threats.title: Supply-chain or release input substitutes malicious code or contracts
preconditions: an unpinned, unreviewed, or compromised source, tool, action, dependency, generator, or signer enters the release
threats.scenario: A trusted-looking artifact contains malicious code or weakened contracts.
mitigations: Protected review, pinned inputs, dependency reconciliation, SBOM, provenance, signatures, and secret scanning.
validations: Clean-clone supply-chain, provenance, signing, and protected-branch negative tests.
threats.residual_risk: A compromised trusted maintainer and signing environment can still collude; independent verification is required.
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: release authority plus non-author security reviewer; critical or high findings are not waivable

threats.title: Public standards publication exposes private or deployment data
preconditions: a secret, private reference, content fixture, active markup, or deployment data path enters a public artifact
threats.scenario: Public documentation or static rendering reveals material that was never meant to leave the deployment or private context.
mitigations: Separate static origin, allowlisted inputs, secret and private-reference scans, safe text rendering, and anonymous review.
validations: Anonymous clone/site scan and active-content tests.
threats.residual_risk: Published Git history is difficult to retract; prevention and review are required.
threats.risk_acceptance_authority: standards authority plus non-author privacy reviewer; critical or high findings are not waivable

legal_hold: A hold records stable ID, organization, actor, authority, reason, scope expression and resolved snapshot, effective time, version, history, and release authorization.
Overlapping holds compose; releasing one does not bypass another.
Relabeling, reprojection, export, backup, or key rotation cannot move governed data outside hold scope.
Hold checks occur at preview, deny-read/new-work point, every destructive phase, key destruction, decommission, and restore.
Emergency or break-glass access may preserve data but cannot silently release or narrow a hold.
Maintain a monotonic organization hold epoch. Hold create, widen, narrow, release, retention apply, deletion, generation destruction, export, and decommission serialize against that epoch.

A destructive operation pins the current hold epoch and resolved lineage under serializable transaction or equivalent fencing. Before each irreversible provider or key action it must reacquire the fence and prove the epoch and scope unchanged; conflict aborts before the action.
An active prospective hold evaluates every new or relabeled record against its versioned scope before the record can become deletable; matching descendants inherit the hold closure.
Crash recovery resumes by operation ID and hold epoch. An uncertain external destructive action remains unknown and blocks completion until reconciled.
Provider preservation is capability-specific. Unsupported, pending, unknown, or contract-only states are reported and cannot be counted as preserved or deleted.
restore: A separately protected signed recovery authority supplies current organization epoch, checkpoint head, key generations, and tombstone watermark.
Before reads, restore compares backup identity and epoch, verifies authority, replays tombstones, and checks required keys and holds.
Missing, stale, forked, wrong-organization, or backup-derived authority keeps affected organizations unreadable and readiness false.
Residual ciphertext in backups is reported honestly; cryptographic erasure means eligible destroyed keys make it infeasible to recover governed plaintext, not that all ciphertext vanished.
limitations: Physical deletion timing depends on storage, backup, replica, recipient, and provider behavior.
Legal-hold requirements vary by jurisdiction and matter; this model is technical research, not legal advice.
Cryptographic erasure is only as strong as key uniqueness, protection, backup discipline, and verified destruction.

rotation: New generation affects new writes only until a resumable rewrap or reindex completes.
Data-root rewrap changes wrapped DEK material and generation, not source digest, receipt, or payload chunk ciphertext.
Search-root rotation dual-writes, reindexes, cuts over, then retires without a query gap.
Secret-root rotation rewraps credentials without readback; audit-root rotation creates a linked signer-generation transition.
Retired generations decrypt existing dependencies but cannot encrypt new material; interruption resumes idempotently under one operation.
destruction: Compute complete organization-scoped dependency and legal-hold closure before authorization.
Require step-up, quorum, separation of duties, current recovery authority, and an attributable operation.
Refuse destruction while source, projection, export, backup requirement, hold, credential, checkpoint, or recovery dependency remains.
Record provider pending, disabled, scheduled, destroyed, purged, unsupported, or unknown state separately.
Never report physical deletion merely because active reads fail or a provider deletion was requested.
restore: Backups contain wrapped material and generation references, never plaintext keys.
Restore compares external recovery authority before unwrapping any root.
Missing eligible key generation keeps governed data unreadable and readiness false; there is no fallback to a development or other-organization provider.
After restore, verify wrong organization, realm, object, field, schema, media type, purpose, generation, and chunk ordinal all fail.
limitations: An authorized or compromised runtime can send roots to its selected cloud KMS, use unwrapped roots, and observe plaintext during processing.
Best-effort memory zeroization cannot guarantee removal from all copies, registers, crash state, or host inspection.
Cloud KMS protects top-level custody but does not make provider or IAM administration infallible.
Destroying a key can make data irrecoverable; it does not remove residual ciphertext or prove every prior plaintext copy is gone.
Real AWS conformance is release-blocking later; GCP and Azure remain contract-tested but real-E2E unverified under the approved exceptions.

global_limitations: This artifact is informative security and privacy research, not a normative protocol, deployment certification, legal opinion, compliance determination, or promise of perfect safety.
Testament cannot provide universal semantic understanding, infer human intent reliably, or guarantee that findings and reviewer decisions are correct.
Application-layer encryption protects persistence boundaries but is not end-to-end encryption against an authorized or compromised runtime processing plaintext.
No-content-egress controls depend on the deployed binary, host, network policy, dependency inventory, and operators; they do not contain host root or out-of-band copying.
External provider behavior, region, retention, training, deletion, and subprocessor claims are declared or observed at the interface, not cryptographically proven by Testament.
GCP Cloud KMS and Azure Key Vault designs are contract-tested only until authorized real resources exist; no real-cloud conformance claim is made.
Hash chains are tamper-evident rather than immutable without independently controlled checkpoints and recovery authority.
Blind indexes intentionally leak bounded equality and frequency information inside one organization.
Legal duties, holds, transfer restrictions, deletion rights, and retention periods depend on role, jurisdiction, contract, purpose, and facts.
The technical processes and controls in version 0.2.0 are proposed research assumptions until accepted public RFCs and ADRs make them normative.
Content-excluding audit and telemetry can still contain personal or linkable identifiers, hashes, timestamps, topology, and legal-hold scope.
